meta.spec_reference: ITU-T Rec. T.81 (09/92) | ISO/IEC 10918-1, 'Information technology - Digital compression and coding of continuous-tone still images - Requirements and guidelines' (the JPEG standard), principally Annex B (compressed data formats) and Annexes C, F and G; JFIF version 1.02 / ITU-T Rec. T.871 (05/2011) for the APP0 segment; Exif version 2.2 (JEITA CP-3451) for the APP1 segment; TIFF Revision 6.0 (Adobe, 1992) for the IFD structure the Exif payload uses; ICC.1:2010 Annex B.4 for the APP2 ICC_PROFILE chunking; Adobe Technical Note 5116 for the APP14 Adobe segment; Adobe Photoshop File Formats Specification for the APP13 image resource blocks; XMP Specification Part 3 for the APP1 XMP segment; Canon CIFF Specification V1R04 for the APP0 HEAPJPGM block; ITU-T Rec. T.87 (06/98) for the JPEG-LS SOF55 frame header; ExifTool's APP12.pm and Photoshop.pm as the reference for the undocumented Ducky and Adobe_CM segments the template cites.

schema_extensions.name: bitfield_layout
schema_extensions.where: every constraints entry whose field is a bitfield - the CIFF tag word, the Exif Flash short, the SOS and DQT nibble pairs, the SOFx and DHP sampling factors, the JFIF version bytes
schema_extensions.why: BitfieldLeftToRight() at lines 56-57 makes the first-declared bitfield member occupy the MOST significant bits. Nothing in the base schema records bit position, yet a generator that packs these fields in declaration order low-to-high produces a byte that is individually legal in every field and completely wrong on disk - it would swap a DC table selector with an AC one, or a horizontal sampling factor with a vertical one. This key names the exact bit range each field occupies.

schema_extensions.name: bit_width
schema_extensions.where: the fixed_value entry for the 9-bit DIRENTRY.unused reserved bitfield
schema_extensions.why: required_value_hex is specified to match the field width, but a 9-bit field has no natural hex width. bit_width states the real width so the hex value is not misread.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead sub-keys: values_hex, comparison, terminates_loop, switch_line, covers_fields, byte_role, additional_call_sites, via, paired_with
schema_extensions.where: the 30 constraints entries that carry a lookahead object
schema_extensions.why: This template's entire dispatch is lookahead-driven and the base lookahead schema cannot express four things it needs. First, most of the literal comparisons go through the helper ReadStringN (lines 96-101) rather than calling ReadBytes directly, so `via` records the indirection a value-mining pass would otherwise miss. Second, the marker dispatch is a switch (line 1545) fed by one peek (line 1544), so `switch_line` separates the peek site from the comparison site. Third, the EOI is located by FindFirst rather than a positional peek and terminates a loop, which `comparison` and `terminates_loop` record. Fourth, the CIFF branch requires TWO literals at two different offsets simultaneously (lines 1148-1149), which `paired_with` records - without it a generator would satisfy only half the guard.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result / fixed_result_hex
schema_extensions.where: the DRI.szSection, APP0.HeaderLength, APP1.offsetFirstIFD, CifDirEntry.data, Huffmann_Table.length, QuanTable.qTable and APP0.palette entries
schema_extensions.why: These fields are both a derived quantity AND an invariant, because the structure they measure is fixed-shape - a DRI segment is always 4 bytes, a quantization table always 64 elements, a JFXX palette always 256 entries. fixed_result records the constant so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what it measures.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout
schema_extensions.where: the CDIR.dirEntries, IFD.dirEntry, APP0.rgb and APP0.palette entries
schema_extensions.why: The per-element stride of these arrays is nowhere stated in the .bt - it is implicit in a struct definition elsewhere - and the rewrite step needs it to convert between an element count and a byte count.

schema_extensions.name: dotted keys for fields inside anonymous nested structs
schema_extensions.where: the CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.*, CDIR.str2Bytes.wData, CDIR.str4Bytes.dwData, DIRENTRY.strAscii.oneByteData, IFD.StrAscii.oneByteData, IFD.strUShort.usValue, IFD.strULong.ulValue, APP12.entry.* and APP13.block.* entries
schema_extensions.why: The schema keys entries as STRUCT_TYPENAME.field_name, but this template declares many structs anonymously and names only the instance - `struct { ... } entry;` at line 1300, `struct { ... } block;` at line 1352, `struct { ... } DC_IMAGESPEC;` at line 697. There is no typename to use. A two-level dotted key names the enclosing typedef'd struct, then the anonymous instance, then the field; every component is a literal identifier from the .bt, so nothing is invented. Several field names (unknown, padding, oneByteData, pixel, App0Type) are also reused across sibling branches of the same struct, and the notes on those entries list every declaration line.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.where: referenced in the UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker notes and in the structure rule for standalone markers
schema_extensions.why: The UNKNOWN branch is defined by exclusion - any 0xFFxx marker the switch has no case for - and separately must exclude the standalone markers that carry no length field. A positive value list cannot express the second exclusion, which is the more dangerous one.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: The .bt disagrees with T.81 in fourteen load-bearing places: two swapped nibble names in the scan component, a mis-named quantization selector, a signed quantization table, duplicate and illegal enum members, fourteen unchecked length subtractions, an unbounded self-recursion, and an UNKNOWN branch that reads a length field from markers that have none. A generator that faithfully imitated the parser's laxity would emit files this template accepts and no real decoder does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

meta.structure_note: A marker stream: the two-byte SOI (0xFFD8), then a sequence of marker segments each introduced by 0xFF plus a code and - for all but the standalone markers - a two-byte big-endian length that counts itself, ending with a scan header (SOS) whose entropy-coded data carries no length at all and runs until the two-byte EOI (0xFFD9) terminates the datastream.

CifDirEntry.storage_method.description: Two-bit CIFF storage class saying whether the entry's value lives in the directory's heap or inline in the entry record itself.
CifDirEntry.storage_method.bitfield_layout: bits 15-14 of the 16-bit tag word, because BitfieldLeftToRight() (lines 56-57) makes the first-declared bitfield occupy the most significant bits
CifDirEntry.storage_method.notes: Enum CIFFTagStg at lines 592-597 names all four encodable values but only 0 and 1 are defined by CIFF; 2 and 3 are explicitly reserved (their names say so). The value selects between two completely different entry layouts at line 576, so it changes the byte length of the record: 8 bytes of sData/oData for kStg_InHeapSpace versus 8 bytes of inline data otherwise. 0 is preferred because it is the branch the template actually decodes at lines 682-736.

CifDirEntry.data_type.description: Three-bit CIFF data-type code; shifted left by 11 it forms the high bits of the CIFFTagDataType constants the template switches on.
CifDirEntry.data_type.bitfield_layout: bits 13-11 of the 16-bit tag word under BitfieldLeftToRight()
CifDirEntry.data_type.notes: Enum CIFFTagDataType at lines 599-607 lists the seven defined values as already-shifted constants (0x0000 through 0x3000 in steps of 0x0800), i.e. this 3-bit field takes 0-6. The value 7 is encodable but undefined. It selects the element width used to size the heap array at lines 700-733, so it changes how many bytes sData describes.

CifDirEntry.id_code.description: Eleven-bit CIFF tag identifier; combined with data_type as (data_type << 11 | id_code) it forms the CIFFTagType constant the template switches on.
CifDirEntry.id_code.bitfield_layout: bits 10-0 of the 16-bit tag word under BitfieldLeftToRight()
CifDirEntry.id_code.notes: The meaningful unit is the full 16-bit combination, not this field alone: enum CIFFTagType at lines 609-644 lists the 30 defined (data_type<<11 | id_code) values. valid_values here is the set of low-11-bit parts of those constants; a generator should instead pick a whole CIFFTagType constant and split it into data_type and id_code so the pair is self-consistent.

CifDirEntry.sData.description: Byte count of this CIFF entry's value in the directory heap; it is what sizes every heap array the template reads.
CifDirEntry.sData.covers: the value bytes at heap offset oData relative to the CIFF directory start; it excludes this size field, the oData field and the entry record itself

generation_range.rationale: A 32-bit byte count used directly as an array bound at lines 703, 708, 713, 718 and 730 with no upper check. Uniform generation asks the parser for up to 4 GB from one 4-byte field. 0-256 bytes per CIFF value keeps the whole APP0 CIFF block in the low kilobytes.

CifDirEntry.sData.notes: Present only when storage_method is kStg_InHeapSpace. The template divides it by 2 for kDT_WORD (line 713) and by 4 for kDT_DWORD (lines 718-719), so for those types it must be an exact multiple of 2 or 4 respectively.

CifDirEntry.oData.description: Offset of this CIFF entry's value, measured from the start of the enclosing CIFF directory, not from the file start.
CifDirEntry.oData.algorithm: relative offset from the enclosing directory's base (the template's local myOffset, set from cDirOffset at line 670)
CifDirEntry.oData.covers: nothing itself; it locates the sData bytes that this entry describes

generation_range.rationale: Fed straight into FSeek at line 684 with no bounds check; a uniform 32-bit value seeks anywhere in a 4 GB address space. Bound it to the size of the CIFF block actually generated.

CifDirEntry.oData.notes: Present only when storage_method is kStg_InHeapSpace. oData + sData must stay inside the directory, i.e. inside cDirSize bytes from cDirOffset.

CifDirEntry.fileFormat.description: CIFF image file-format code, read only for the kTC_ImageFormat tag.

generation_range.rationale: Only a handful of low-numbered format codes are defined; huge values are meaningless and add no coverage.

CifDirEntry.fileFormat.notes: Reached only through `case kTC_ImageFormat:` at line 581, i.e. when (data_type << 11 | id_code) equals 0x1803.

CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.description: CIFF target compression ratio accompanying the image-format code; a positive IEEE-754 single-precision ratio.

generation_range.rationale: A compression ratio; NaN, infinity and absurd magnitudes are what uniform 32-bit generation produces and they exercise nothing.

CifDirEntry.data.description: The eight bytes of inline value data carried in the entry record itself when the storage class is not kStg_InHeapSpace.
CifDirEntry.data.covers: the eight bytes occupying the same record positions that sData and oData occupy in the heap-storage layout
CifDirEntry.data.notes: CIFF stores values of eight bytes or fewer inline; this is why both entry layouts are exactly 10 bytes long (2 tag + 8 value).

CDIR.nDirEntry.description: Number of CifDirEntry records in this CIFF directory; it is the array bound for dirEntries and must match the record count exactly.
CDIR.nDirEntry.covers: the CifDirEntry dirEntries[] array that immediately follows it; it excludes this count field and the trailing szValues field

generation_range.rationale: Each entry is 10 bytes and may point at up to sData bytes of heap. A 16-bit count of 65535 entries is 640 KB of records plus unbounded heap, from one 2-byte field. 0-16 entries keeps a CIFF directory small.

CDIR.dirEntries.description: The CIFF directory record array; its element count is nDirEntry and each element is a fixed 10 bytes.
CDIR.dirEntries.algorithm: element count = CDIR.nDirEntry; byte count = 10 * nDirEntry
CDIR.dirEntries.covers: the directory records between nDirEntry and szValues
CDIR.dirEntries.byte_layout: 10 bytes per record: a 16-bit packed tag word (storage_method:2, data_type:3, id_code:11) followed by 8 bytes of either sData+oData or inline data

CDIR.szValues.description: Offset from the directory base to the directory record block; the template reads the same value by lookahead as the local S and seeks to cDirOffset + S before parsing.
CDIR.szValues.algorithm: relative offset from the CIFF directory base to the start of the directory records, i.e. the size of the heap value area that precedes them
CDIR.szValues.covers: the heap value area preceding the record block; it excludes the record block and this field itself

generation_range.rationale: Used as a seek target at line 672; bound it to the generated CIFF block size.

CDIR.szValues.notes: The template's inline comment says '= S', and S is read at line 671 as ReadInt(myOffset + cDirSize - 4), i.e. this same DWORD located as the last four bytes of the directory. So szValues is simultaneously the last field of the structure and the value the parser needed before it could locate the structure - a generator must emit it in both roles consistently.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.description: Image width in pixels recorded in the CIFF kTC_ImageSpec property.

generation_range.rationale: A metadata dimension; uniform 32-bit values are absurd and some readers allocate from them.

evidence.note: CIFF specification V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec (0x1810): the property is seven 32-bit fields beginning with image width and height in pixels. The template reads it as a plain DC_UINT32 with no check.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.description: Image height in pixels recorded in the CIFF kTC_ImageSpec property.

generation_range.rationale: Same metadata-dimension reasoning as imageWidth.

evidence.note: CIFF V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec: the second 32-bit field is the image height in pixels. The template performs no check.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.rotationAngle.description: Rotation to apply to the CIFF image, in degrees; only the four right-angle rotations are meaningful.

evidence.note: CIFF V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec: the rotation angle field records the display rotation in degrees; cameras write only 0, 90, 180 or 270. The template reads a signed 32-bit integer with no check.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.componentBitDepth.description: Bits per colour component in the CIFF image spec.

evidence.note: CIFF V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec: component bit depth records bits per component; camera values are 8, 10, 12 or 16. The template performs no check.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.colorBitDepth.description: Total bits per pixel across all colour components in the CIFF image spec.

evidence.note: CIFF V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec: colour bit depth is the total bits per pixel and is componentBitDepth times the component count. The template performs no check.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.colorBW.description: Flag distinguishing a colour CIFF image from a black-and-white one.

evidence.note: CIFF V1R04, kTC_ImageSpec: the final 32-bit field is a colour/black-and-white indicator. The template reads a plain DC_UINT32 with no check.

CDIR.str2Bytes.wData.description: CIFF heap value read as an array of 16-bit words; its element count is the entry's byte size divided by two, so that size must be even.
CDIR.str2Bytes.wData.algorithm: element count = CifDirEntry.sData / 2, requiring sData to be an exact multiple of 2
CDIR.str2Bytes.wData.covers: the sData bytes at heap offset oData for an entry whose data_type is kDT_WORD
CDIR.str2Bytes.wData.notes: The shift truncates rather than rejecting an odd sData, so an odd size silently drops the last byte and desynchronises the heap.

CDIR.str4Bytes.dwData.description: CIFF heap value read as an array of 32-bit words; its element count is the entry's byte size divided by four, so that size must be a multiple of four.
CDIR.str4Bytes.dwData.algorithm: element count = CifDirEntry.sData / 4, requiring sData to be an exact multiple of 4
CDIR.str4Bytes.dwData.covers: the sData bytes at heap offset oData for an entry whose data_type is kDT_DWORD
CDIR.str4Bytes.dwData.notes: dwData and flData at lines 718-719 are two members of a union covering the same bytes; a generator must write them once, not twice.

DIRENTRY.tagNumber.description: 16-bit TIFF/Exif tag identifier; which enum it is drawn from depends on which kind of IFD the parser is currently inside.
DIRENTRY.tagNumber.notes: Three separate enums can supply this field, chosen at lines 764-774 by the top of the parser's IFD-type stack: ExifTag (lines 169-496, 325 values) for a normal or Exif or Interop IFD, GeoTag (lines 498-530, 31 values, 0x0000-0x001E) for the GPS IFD reached through the GPSInfo tag, and CasioTag2 (lines 534-563, 28 values) for a Casio QV-R62 MakerNote IFD. valid_values above lists the practical Exif working set; the full legal set is the union of the three enums. TIFF 6.0 additionally requires the entries of an IFD to be sorted in ascending tag order, which nothing here checks.

DIRENTRY.dataFormat.description: TIFF data-type code selecting the element width of this entry's value; only 1 through 12 are defined and the template's own guard rejects anything outside that range.
DIRENTRY.dataFormat.notes: Enum tagDataFormat at lines 746-759. The parallel table dataFormatLength at line 744 gives the byte width of each code as {0,1,1,2,4,8,1,1,2,4,8,4,8}, indexed by the code, and the guards at lines 780 and 786 require 1 <= dataFormat < 13. This field is what turns nComponent into a byte count, so it decides whether the entry's value is stored inline in the 4-byte value slot or out of line at offsetData.

DIRENTRY.nComponent.description: Number of elements of type dataFormat in this entry's value; multiplied by the type width it gives the value's byte length.
DIRENTRY.nComponent.algorithm: element count; byte length = dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent
DIRENTRY.nComponent.covers: the entry's value bytes - held inline in the 4-byte value slot when the product is 4 or less, otherwise held at absolute position offset + offsetData; it excludes the tagNumber, dataFormat and nComponent fields themselves

generation_range.rationale: A 32-bit element count multiplied by up to 8 bytes per element and used directly as an array bound at lines 967-1023 with no upper check. Uniform generation asks for up to 32 GB from one 4-byte field. 1-64 elements bounds every Exif value at 512 bytes while still crossing the 4-byte inline/out-of-line boundary.

DIRENTRY.nComponent.notes: For dataFormat ascString the count includes the terminating NUL, so an empty string still has nComponent 1.

DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.description: Exif exposure-program code, read inline when the tag number is ExposureProgram (0x8822).
DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.notes: Anonymous enum at lines 789-799. Exif 2.2 defines exactly these nine values for tag 0x8822.

DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.description: Exif metering-mode code, read inline when the tag number is MeteringMode (0x9207).
DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.notes: Anonymous enum at lines 802-811. Note the gap: 7-254 are reserved and only 255 ('other') is legal above 6.

DIRENTRY.LightSource.description: Exif light-source code, read inline when the tag number is LightSource (0x9208).
DIRENTRY.LightSource.notes: Anonymous enum at lines 814-836. The set is deliberately gappy: 5-8 and 16 are unassigned, the block 17-24 is the explicit-illuminant range, and 255 is 'other'.

DIRENTRY.unused.description: The nine unused high bits of the Exif Flash bitfield (tag 0x9209); the specification assigns no meaning to them, so they are written as zero.
DIRENTRY.unused.bitfield_layout: bits 15-7 of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()
DIRENTRY.unused.notes: Exif 2.2 tag 0x9209 defines only the low seven bits of the Flash short; the template names the remainder 'unused'.

DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.description: Exif Flash red-eye-reduction bit: 1 means red-eye reduction was supported or used.
value_names: no red-eye reduction mode or unknown
DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.bitfield_layout: bit 6 of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()

DIRENTRY.flash_function.description: Exif Flash function-present bit: 1 means no flash function is present on the camera.
DIRENTRY.flash_function.bitfield_layout: bit 5 of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()

DIRENTRY.flash_mode.description: Exif Flash mode: two bits recording the camera's flash firing mode.
DIRENTRY.flash_mode.bitfield_layout: bits 4-3 of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()

DIRENTRY.flash_return.description: Exif Flash return-light status: two bits recording whether strobe return light was detected.
DIRENTRY.flash_return.bitfield_layout: bits 2-1 of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()
DIRENTRY.flash_return.notes: Exif 2.2 leaves the encoding 1 reserved, so only 0, 2 and 3 are legal even though the field is two bits wide.

DIRENTRY.flash_fired.description: Exif Flash fired bit: 1 means the flash fired.
DIRENTRY.flash_fired.bitfield_layout: bit 0 (least significant) of the 16-bit Flash value under BitfieldLeftToRight()

DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.description: Exif exposure-mode code, read inline when the tag number is ExposureMode (0xa402).

DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.description: Exif white-balance code, read inline when the tag number is WhiteBalance (0xa403).

DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.description: Exif scene-capture-type code, read inline when the tag number is SceneCaptureType (0xa406).

DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.description: Exif subject-distance-range code, read inline when the tag number is SubjectDistanceRange (0xa40c).

DIRENTRY.strAscii.oneByteData.description: Inline value bytes of an Exif entry whose total length is 4 or less; the element count is nComponent.
DIRENTRY.strAscii.oneByteData.algorithm: element count = DIRENTRY.nComponent, with dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent constrained to at most 4
DIRENTRY.strAscii.oneByteData.covers: the inline value bytes occupying the entry's 4-byte value slot

generation_range.rationale: This branch is only reached when the total value length is 4 bytes or fewer, so the count is bounded by the type width.

DIRENTRY.strAscii.oneByteData.notes: Declared three times over for dataFormat uByte (line 879), ascString (line 884, inside the named struct StrAscii1) and undefined (line 889).

DIRENTRY.usValue.description: Inline 16-bit value of an Exif entry of type uShort; the template emits one per component in a loop.
DIRENTRY.usValue.algorithm: repeated DIRENTRY.nComponent times, bounded by the 4-byte inline slot so nComponent is at most 2
DIRENTRY.usValue.covers: the inline value slot of an entry whose dataFormat is uShort

generation_range.rationale: Two 16-bit values are the most that fit in the 4-byte inline slot.

DIRENTRY.usValue.notes: Read back at line 1204 as ifdThumbnailImage.dirEntry[i].usValue to obtain the thumbnail's Compression value, so for the Compression tag this field decides whether the thumbnail is parsed as JPEG.

DIRENTRY.ulValue.description: Inline 32-bit value of an Exif entry of type uLong1 or sLong; for the pointer tags it is an offset from the TIFF header base that the template seeks to.
DIRENTRY.ulValue.algorithm: absolute offset from the TIFF header base (the local `offset` captured at line 1180, i.e. the first byte after 'Exif\0\0') when the tag is a pointer tag; otherwise a plain 32-bit value
DIRENTRY.ulValue.covers: nothing itself; for ExifOffset, GPSInfo, InteropOffset, MakerNote and CasioPreviewThumbnail it locates the sub-IFD or thumbnail that follows

generation_range.rationale: Fed straight into FSeek at lines 1034, 1040, 1046, 1054 and 1064 with no bounds check. A uniform 32-bit value seeks anywhere in a 4 GB space; bound it to the size of the APP1 segment actually generated, whose own length field caps it at 65535 anyway.

DIRENTRY.ulValue.notes: Present only when nComponent is 1 (guards at lines 897 and 911). Also read back at lines 1208 and 1212 to locate and size the Exif thumbnail.

DIRENTRY.padding.description: Filler bytes that pad an inline Exif value out to the full 4-byte value slot; TIFF leaves them undefined and encoders write zero.
DIRENTRY.padding.notes: Emitted at line 922 only when the computed value length is not exactly 4, so the array is 1 to 3 bytes long. Its size is 4 - dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent, which makes the entry a fixed 12 bytes regardless of type: 2 tag + 2 format + 4 count + 4 value slot.

DIRENTRY.offsetData.description: Offset from the TIFF header base to this entry's value, used instead of an inline value whenever the value exceeds 4 bytes.
DIRENTRY.offsetData.algorithm: offset from the TIFF header base (the local `offset` captured at line 1180, the first byte after the 'Exif\0\0' identifier)
DIRENTRY.offsetData.covers: nothing itself; it locates the dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent value bytes that this entry describes

generation_range.rationale: Used as an FSeek target at line 961 with no bounds check. The enclosing APP1 segment cannot exceed 65535 bytes, so any larger offset points outside the segment; bound it to the generated segment size.

DIRENTRY.offsetData.notes: Occupies the same 4 bytes as the inline value slot - the two are alternatives chosen by the guard at line 786, never both. TIFF 6.0 requires the value to begin on an even byte boundary and to lie inside the TIFF block.

IFD.nDirEntry.description: Number of 12-byte directory entries in this IFD; it is the array bound for dirEntry and must match the entry count exactly.
IFD.nDirEntry.covers: the DIRENTRY dirEntry[] array that immediately follows it; it excludes this count field and the trailing nextIFDoffset

generation_range.rationale: Each entry is 12 bytes and may point at up to nComponent * 8 further bytes. A 16-bit count of 65535 entries is 786 KB of entry records alone, inside an APP1 segment whose length field cannot exceed 65535 - so large values are not merely slow, they are self-contradictory. 1-16 entries keeps an IFD small and internally consistent.

IFD.dirEntry.description: The IFD entry array; its element count is nDirEntry and each element is exactly 12 bytes.
IFD.dirEntry.algorithm: element count = IFD.nDirEntry; byte count = 12 * nDirEntry
IFD.dirEntry.covers: the entry records between nDirEntry and nextIFDoffset
IFD.dirEntry.byte_layout: 12 bytes per entry: 2-byte tagNumber, 2-byte dataFormat, 4-byte nComponent, then either the inline value plus padding or a 4-byte offsetData
IFD.dirEntry.notes: TIFF 6.0 requires the entries to be sorted in ascending tagNumber order; nothing in the template checks this.

IFD.nextIFDoffset.description: Offset from the TIFF header base to the next IFD in the chain, or 0 to end the chain; a non-zero value here is what makes the template parse a thumbnail IFD.
IFD.nextIFDoffset.algorithm: offset from the TIFF header base (the local `offset` captured at line 1180); 0 terminates the IFD chain
IFD.nextIFDoffset.covers: nothing itself; it locates the next IFD structure

generation_range.rationale: Seeked to at line 1192 with no bounds check. 0 is by far the most productive value: it terminates the chain cleanly. Any non-zero value must point at a real IFD inside the same APP1 segment, so it is capped by the segment's own 16-bit length.

IFD.nextIFDoffset.notes: A self-referential or backward offset makes a decoder loop; TIFF 6.0 requires the chain to be acyclic and forward-moving.

IFD.StrAscii.oneByteData.description: Out-of-line ASCII value of an Exif entry; its byte count is the entry's nComponent and the string must end in a NUL.
IFD.StrAscii.oneByteData.covers: the value bytes at absolute position offset + DIRENTRY.offsetData

generation_range.rationale: Mirrors the nComponent generation bound; Exif ASCII values are short in practice.

IFD.StrAscii.oneByteData.notes: Exif 2.2 requires an ASCII value to be NUL-terminated and counts the NUL in nComponent, so the final byte must be 0.

IFD.strUShort.usValue.description: Out-of-line array of 16-bit Exif values; its element count is the entry's nComponent.
IFD.strUShort.usValue.algorithm: element count = DIRENTRY.nComponent; byte count = 2 * nComponent
IFD.strUShort.usValue.covers: the value bytes at absolute position offset + DIRENTRY.offsetData

generation_range.rationale: This branch is reached only when the value exceeds 4 bytes, so at least 3 components; capped with nComponent.

IFD.strULong.ulValue.description: Out-of-line array of 32-bit Exif values; its element count is the entry's nComponent.
IFD.strULong.ulValue.algorithm: element count = DIRENTRY.nComponent; byte count = 4 * nComponent
IFD.strULong.ulValue.covers: the value bytes at absolute position offset + DIRENTRY.offsetData

generation_range.rationale: Reached only when the value exceeds 4 bytes, so at least 2 components.

URatio.uRValue.description: Out-of-line array of unsigned TIFF RATIONAL values, each a numerator and denominator pair of 32-bit unsigned integers.
URatio.uRValue.algorithm: element count = DIRENTRY.nComponent; byte count = 8 * nComponent
URatio.uRValue.covers: the value bytes at absolute position offset + DIRENTRY.offsetData

generation_range.rationale: Each element is 8 bytes; Exif rationals are used in short arrays such as the three-element GPS coordinate.

URatio.uRValue.notes: The denominator must not be zero: TIFF 6.0 defines a RATIONAL as num/den and every Exif reader divides by den when formatting the value, so a zero denominator is a division fault waiting in the decoder. The template never checks it.

generation_range.rationale: Same frame-buffer allocation blow-up as Y_image; the product of the two is what a decoder reserves, so both must be capped together.

SOFx.X_image.notes: ITU-T T.81 B.2.2: 'X: Number of samples per line - Specifies the maximum number of samples per line in the source image ... 1 <= X <= 65535.'

COMPS.Vert.description: Vertical sampling factor of this component; a value of 0 is a division by zero in the MCU geometry.
COMPS.Vert.bitfield_layout: the low nibble of the second COMPS byte under BitfieldLeftToRight()
COMPS.Vert.notes: ITU-T T.81 B.2.2: 'Vi: Vertical sampling factor ... 1 <= Vi <= 4.' Subject to the same ten-data-unit MCU cap as COMPS.Horz.

JPGFILE.SOIMarker.notes: ITU-T T.81 B.1.1.3 and Table B.1: SOI = 0xFFD8 is a standalone marker with no parameters. Together with the following marker it forms the file's identifying bytes, which the template header records at line 11 as 'FF D8 FF'. This is the single most important fixed value in the format and must never receive an evil value.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.description: End Of Image: the two bytes that terminate the datastream, located by a forward search from the start of the scan data.

lookahead.note: This is the only search-based marker location in the template. Its result decides the length of the scan data: found means scanData runs up to it, not found (fpos2 < 0) means the rest of the file is consumed as unterminatedScanData and a warning is printed.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.notes: ITU-T T.81 B.1.1.3 and Table B.1: EOI = 0xFFD9 is a standalone marker with no parameters. Omitting it does not stop this template - the fpos2 < 0 branch at lines 1554-1558 handles it - but it makes the file truncated for every real decoder. Because the search is a plain forward byte scan, any 0xFFD9 pair appearing inside the entropy-coded data will be mistaken for the terminator, which is the failure the 1.6.2 history entry at line 15 describes.

JPGFILE.scanData.description: The entropy-coded image data between the scan header and the EOI marker; its length is not stored anywhere and must be discovered by scanning.
JPGFILE.scanData.algorithm: byte count = the file position of the first 0xFFD9 pair at or after the current position, minus the current position
JPGFILE.scanData.covers: every byte from the end of the SOS header up to but not including the EOI marker

generation_range.rationale: This is the only unbounded region of a JPEG that carries no length field at all - it runs until a marker is found - so it is the format's principal size lever. 8 KB of scan data keeps generated files small while still producing a plausible entropy-coded segment.

JPGFILE.scanData.notes: The bytes are constrained in one crucial way the template does not model: inside entropy-coded data a literal 0xFF byte must be followed by a 0x00 stuffing byte (T.81 F.1.2.3, 'byte stuffing'), because any other following byte is read as a marker. A generator emitting uniform random bytes will produce roughly one accidental marker every 256 bytes, truncating the scan. Stuffing every 0xFF is the single highest-value thing a generator can do for this field. The only markers legally allowed to appear inside the scan are RST0-RST7, and only when DRI.Ri is non-zero.

JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.description: The scan data of a file with no EOI marker at all; the template consumes everything to the end of the file and warns.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.algorithm: byte count = JpegFileEnd - FTell(), i.e. everything remaining to the end of the file (or to the end of the enclosing thumbnail region for a nested parse)
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.covers: every byte from the end of the SOS header to the end of the file

generation_range.rationale: Reached only when no EOI is present, which a generator should avoid entirely; bounded together with scanData.

JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.notes: Reached when FindFirst returns a negative position at line 1554. A generator should never produce this shape: it means the file has no EOI and is truncated for every decoder.

JPGFILE.unknownPadding.description: Bytes appearing after the EOI marker; a conforming JPEG datastream has none.
JPGFILE.unknownPadding.algorithm: byte count = JpegFileEnd - FTell() after the EOI marker has been consumed
JPGFILE.unknownPadding.covers: every trailing byte between the EOI marker and the end of the file

generation_range.rationale: A conforming datastream ends at EOI. Trailing bytes are tolerated by most decoders but are not part of the format, and they cost file size for no coverage.

JPGFILE.unknownPadding.notes: Emitted only when the guard `if(JpegFileEnd - FTell())` at line 1565 finds trailing bytes; the template colours them silver to mark them as padding.

structure.subject: 0xFF00 as a marker
structure.detail: the byte pair 0xFF 0x00 is not a marker - it is a stuffed 0xFF data byte - and 0xFFFF is a fill sequence, not a marker either
structure.description: These two exclusions are what make byte stuffing work; a generator that treats every 0xFFxx pair as a marker will corrupt scan data.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is an exclusion, not a repeating element
structure.generation_note: when writing scan data, follow every emitted 0xFF with 0x00; when writing markers, never emit code 0x00 or 0xFF

template_deviations.subject: M_ID enum, M_JPG14 and M_JPG15
template_deviations.issue: The M_JPG0 block at lines 159-161 runs M_JPG0 = 0xFFF0 through M_JPG15 = 0xFFFF, which makes M_JPG14 equal 0xFFFE - the same value as M_COMM declared at line 162 - and M_JPG15 equal 0xFFFF, which is a fill sequence and not a marker at all. T.81 defines JPG0-JPG13 only, at 0xFFF0-0xFFFD.
template_deviations.impact: Two duplicate/illegal enum members. A generator drawing uniformly from M_ID can emit 0xFFFF as a 'marker', which the template's own fill-byte skip at line 1542 would then eat.
template_deviations.action: Treat 0xFFF0-0xFFFD as the JPGn range and exclude 0xFFFE (COM) and 0xFFFF from any generated marker set.

template_deviations.subject: COMPSOS.AC and COMPSOS.DC
template_deviations.issue: The two nibbles are named the wrong way round. T.81 B.2.3 puts Td, the DC entropy table selector, in the HIGH nibble and Ta, the AC selector, in the LOW nibble. With BitfieldLeftToRight() in force (lines 56-57) the first-declared field occupies the high nibble, so the field the template calls AC is really the DC selector and vice versa.
template_deviations.impact: A generator that reads these names literally will swap the two table selectors in every scan component.
template_deviations.action: Emit the high nibble as the DC table index and the low nibble as the AC table index, whatever the fields are called.

template_deviations.subject: COMPS.compNr
template_deviations.issue: Named as though it were a component number, but at this byte position T.81 B.2.2 places Tqi, the quantization table destination selector, whose legal range is 0-3.
template_deviations.impact: A generator treating it as a free component index will emit values 4-255 that every real decoder rejects, while this template accepts them silently.
template_deviations.action: Constrain to 0-3 and tie it to a quantization table actually installed by a DQT segment.

template_deviations.subject: every szSection field
template_deviations.issue: Fourteen separate segment structs read a 16-bit length and then subtract a constant from it to size a trailing array - szSection - 2, - 8, - 11, - 12, - 16 or - 31 - with no check that the length is large enough. Several structs (SOFx, SOS, DHP, DRI) do not use the length at all and read their fields by shape instead.
template_deviations.impact: On malformed input the array sizes go negative. For generation it means the length and the payload must be chosen together, and that a wrong length in SOFx, SOS, DHP or DRI is invisible to this template while being fatal to a real decoder, which skips exactly szSection bytes.
template_deviations.action: Always generate the payload first and derive the length from it; never draw a length independently.

template_deviations.subject: the top-level marker loop
template_deviations.issue: while(FTell() < JpegFileEnd && !bEOI) has no requirement that the first marker be SOI, no requirement that a frame header precede a scan, and a single-byte resynchronisation branch at line 1621 that swallows arbitrary junk between segments.
template_deviations.impact: The template will happily parse a file with no SOI, no SOF and no DQT - a file no decoder accepts. Its laxity says nothing about validity.
template_deviations.action: Treat SOI-first, SOF-before-SOS and EOI-last as hard structural requirements during generation.

template_deviations.subject: JPGFILE.scanData and the EOI search
template_deviations.issue: The scan extent is found by FindFirst for the byte pair 0xFFD9 rather than by a proper marker scan that honours byte stuffing. The 1.6.2 history entry at line 15 records that this was changed from a backward to a forward search precisely because the data can contain bytes that look like the marker.
template_deviations.impact: Any accidental 0xFFD9 inside the entropy-coded data truncates the scan. A generator emitting unstuffed random bytes hits this roughly once every 65536 bytes, and hits an accidental marker of some kind roughly every 256 bytes.
template_deviations.action: Emit scan data with every 0xFF followed by 0x00, which makes an accidental marker impossible.

template_deviations.subject: Huffmann_Table.length and HTV
template_deviations.issue: The sixteen BITS counts are summed at lines 1423-1427 with no check that the sum is at most 256, that the counts describe a valid prefix code, or that a DC table has at most 16 symbols.
template_deviations.impact: Uniform generation of the sixteen bytes sums to roughly 2040, producing an HTV array eight times the legal maximum that swallows the following segments.
template_deviations.action: Generate the total symbol count first (at most 256, or 16 for a DC table), then partition it across the sixteen lengths.

template_deviations.subject: QuanTable.Pq
template_deviations.issue: The precision nibble is tested as `if (Pq == 0)` so every one of the fourteen encodable-but-illegal values 2-15 falls into the else branch and doubles the table to 128 bytes.
template_deviations.impact: A single out-of-range nibble silently changes the segment size by 64 bytes and desynchronises the DQT table loop.
template_deviations.action: Constrain Pq to 0 or 1, and to 0 whenever the frame's sample precision is 8.

template_deviations.subject: QuanTable.qTable 8-bit form
template_deviations.issue: Declared as `byte qTable[64]` - a SIGNED type - where T.81 specifies unsigned 8-bit quantization values in the range 1-255.
template_deviations.impact: Coefficients above 127 display as negative, and a generator respecting the declared signed type would produce only half the legal range.

template_deviations.subject: JPGLS component records
template_deviations.issue: The struct reads exactly one component record (C_compID, sub_sampling, Tq at lines 1514-1516) regardless of what Nf says, and dumps the remainder into uknown[].
template_deviations.impact: A multi-component JPEG-LS frame is mis-parsed, and the template's own output is inconsistent with its own Nf field.
template_deviations.action: Emit Nf = 1 for a self-consistent JPEG-LS frame, or generate 3 * Nf bytes of component records and let the tail absorb them.

template_deviations.subject: UNKNOWN and the standalone markers
template_deviations.issue: The UNKNOWN struct unconditionally reads a two-byte length after the marker. RST0-RST7 (0xFFD0-0xFFD7), TEM (0xFF01) and EOI have no length field, so routing one here consumes two bytes of the following data as a phantom length.
template_deviations.impact: This is the template's most destructive desynchronisation path: one standalone marker in the wrong place shifts the parse of the entire rest of the file.
template_deviations.action: Never emit a standalone marker where the dispatch would route it to UNKNOWN.

template_deviations.subject: enum IFD_dirtype
template_deviations.issue: Declared at lines 73-77 but no field in the file ever has this type. It exists only as parse state: the values are pushed onto the local string stack_IFD_dirtype and read back at line 764 to choose which tag enum applies to DIRENTRY.tagNumber.
template_deviations.impact: None for generation - there are no bytes to emit. It is recorded here so its absence from the constraints map reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
template_deviations.action: Model it as generator state: the IFD kind currently being emitted, which selects the tag vocabulary.

template_deviations.subject: nested JPGFILE recursion
template_deviations.issue: JPGFILE instantiates itself at lines 1126, 1222 and 1068 with no depth limit; each nested parse re-enters the same unbounded marker loop with JpegFileEnd temporarily narrowed.
template_deviations.impact: Unbounded recursion is the fastest route from this template to a non-terminating or enormous generation, because each level multiplies the segment budget.
template_deviations.action: Cap the nesting depth at 1 and bound each nested datastream explicitly.

template_deviations.subject: BitfieldLeftToRight and the double endian call
template_deviations.issue: Lines 56-57 call LittleEndian() then BigEndian(), each followed by BitfieldLeftToRight(). Only the second endian setting survives, so the file is parsed big-endian - but the bit order is set for both, which is the point of the redundant pair.
template_deviations.impact: Every bitfield in the template packs first-declared into the MOST significant bits. A generator packing the other way produces bytes that are individually 'legal' in every field and completely wrong on disk.
template_deviations.action: Pack all bitfields high-to-low in declaration order; note that the Exif TIFF block and the CIFF block temporarily switch to little-endian based on their own byte-order marks.
